items.e: MOREOVER THOU SHALT MAKE THE TABERNACLE. As you were first told, namely, the pattern of the tabernacle (Ex. 25:9).

THE WORK OF THE SKILLFUL WORKMAN. Our sages said that ma’aseh choshev (the work of the skillful workman) refers to two faces, and [ ma’aseh ] rokem (the work of the weaver) (v. 36) to one image. What they said is correct. However, according to the plain meaning of the text, ma’aseh choshev is neither needle-work nor weaving. It refers rather to a process employed today in making silk garments. The image that arises in the heart comes from insight and thought. The artist draws it upon a tablet. He then places two threads upon the image which he thought up in order to draw it from a distance.

THE LENGTH. The uninformed say that the curtains were twenty-eight cubits in length because of the twenty-eight stages of the moon. However, actually there were ten curtains over the tabernacle to correspond with Who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain (Ps. 104:2). The place of the Holy of Holies therefore was a cube in measure.

COUPLED. Choverot (coupled) is an adjective. On the other hand, it might be a verb meaning that this curtain coupled the other curtain. Ephraim is joined (chavur) to idols (Hos. 4:17), wherein chavur is a pu’al , is proof of the aforementioned.

LOOPS. Some say that the word u-ve-lullim (and by winding stairs) in and they went up by winding stairs into the middle row (I Kings 6:8) is similar to the word lule’ot (loops), for the bet in u-ve-lullim is a preposition.
THAT IS OUTMOST. The word ha-kitzonah (that is outmost) is an adjective like the word ha-elyonah (that is uppermost).
FIFTY. Scripture now mentions the number of loops.

[OPPOSITE.] The word makbilot (opposite) means this one was opposite the other. There are those who say that the word koval (before) in and smote him before the people (II Kings 15:10) and kavolo (opposite it) in and shall strike that which is opposite it (Ezek. 26:9) are similar.
[ONE.] The word ishah (one) means the very thing. The same is true with the word ish (man). Scripture therefore reads, ve-ha-ish gavri’el (the man Gabriel) (Dan. 9:21).
AND THOU SHALT MAKE FIFTY CLASPS OF GOLD. The word kores (stoopeth) in Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth (Is. 46:1) is similar.

[THAT THE TABERNACLE MAY BE ONE WHOLE.] Look, the term tabernacle refers to the ten curtains. The tabernacle is called one, and it encompass all ten [curtains] for all physical entities are made of various elements. Similarly God the revered, who is One. God includes everything and is called One. The same is true with the microcosm and the macrocosm.
AND THOU SHALT MAKE CURTAINS OF GOATS’ HAIR FOR A TENT. Le-ohel (for a tent) means to serve as a tent.
[THEM.] The word otam (them) is there for purposes of additional explanation, as it refers to the curtains of goats’ hair.

THE LENGTH OF EACH CURTAIN. The word achat (each) is irregular. The word should have read achedet , for the dalet is not a letter that serves as a prefix or a suffix. However, the dalet was dropped because it is very hard to sound a dalet and a tav , both of which are dentals, back to back. It was dropped for the same reason that the tav in mesharat (ministered) in ministered unto the king (II Kings 1:15) was dropped.
FIVE. The word chamesh (five) is vocalized with a sheva and a pattach . It is an abridged form, like the word shelosh (three) in shelosh se’im (three measures) (Gen. 18:6).

[AND SHALT DOUBLE OVER THE SIXTH CURTAIN IN THE FOREFRONT OF THE TENT.] Observe, when the sixth curtain was doubled, half of a curtain was left at the end. Hence Scripture states, the half curtain that remaineth over (v. 12). There is no need to mention that the length of the curtains was placed over the width of the tabernacle. Now the width of the tabernacle was ten cubits, and the height of its two sides was nine cubits. Scripture therefore states, And the cubit on the one side (v. 13) to cover the tabernacle.

AND THOU SHALT MAKE FIFTY LOOPS. The number of loops on the curtains of the tent was the same as the number of loops of the tabernacle. The same applies to the clasps. However, the loops and the clasps of the tent were not opposite the loops and the clasps of the tabernacle. On the contrary, they were two cubits behind them towards the west.
AND THOU SHALT MAKE. The clasps of the curtains which made up the tabernacle were made of gold because they were used for the most important curtains.
The tent served as a cover over the tabernacle. Its clasps were therefore made of brass. The brass clasps were not visible because there were two covers over the tent.

AND AS FOR THE OVERHANGING PART…THE HALF CURTAIN. The term half is sometimes used in the sense of close to a half, as in and the half-tribe of Manasseh (Josh. 22:9). When we come to the description of the boards you will understand that which requires explanation.
AND THE CUBIT…WHICH REMAINETH OVER. The word ba-odef (which remaineth over) is like the word oved (perishing). It is an adjective, as the cantillical note is placed on the last syllable.
AND THOU SHALT MAKE A COVERING. Over the covering because of the rain.
AND THOU SHALT MAKE THE BOARDS FOR THE TABERNACLE. The term tabernacle only applies to the curtains and the boards. As God informed Moses of the tabernacle, so did He inform him of the boards.

[STANDING UP.] The word omedim means standing up as it grew on the tree, for the length of the wood is its height. The same applies to a person when he stands. The opposite is the case when he lies down. On the other hand, the word omedim might mean standing straight up.

TEN CUBITS. We do not know whether the cubits of the tabernacle were measured from the armpits like Ezekiel’s cubits. Logically, the cubits of the first temple were of such cubits, as we find that the Book Of Chronicles speaks of the earlier measure.
TWO TENONS. The word yadot (tenons) comes from the same root as yad (hands).
JOINED. The word meshullavot (joined) has no cognate except for the word ha-shelabbim (the stays) (I Kings 7:29).

AND THOU SHALT MAKE. Observe! Scripture does not record the thickness of the boards. The ancients said that each board was a cubit thick. If this is the case then the southern wall, which was thirty cubits, [was a cubit thick]. This was also the case with the northern wall. Thus a space measuring eight cubits in width was left for the western wall. However, eight boards had to be placed there. It is possible that the ancients were compelled to say that the boards were a cubit thick. They were compelled to say that the boards were a cubit thick because of the middle bar which was inserted into the boards. According to Rabbi Solomon the bar could only lay there by a miracle. According to the plain meaning of the text there were three middle bars. Scripture similarly writes, from end to end (v. 28). It does not state from end to the ends. Now if the sages received a tradition that the boards were a cubit in thickness, then we will accept their tradition. However, if they arrived at this measurement by reasoning, then we can explain it differently. The two bars, namely, the upper two bars, and likewise the two lower bars, reached half of the wall. The middle bar that was placed in the midst (be-tokh) of the boards (v. 28) passed through from end to end. To work it in the midst (be-tokh) of the blue, and in the midst of the purple (Ex. 39:3) is similar, as is and put the bells in the midst (be-tokh) of the pomegranates (Ex. 39:25). The middle bars would not have been covered with gold if they were not placed on the surface of the boards. If we admit that we do not know the thickness of each board, then we can explain the structure of the western wall. Now, they first set up the western wall. For two boards were set aside to serve as corners of the tabernacle, as the meaning of mekutzot is corners. The same was true of half of the corners of the courtyard, for the courtyard was in the form of a parallelogram. We thus have two corners. Now these two corner boards were not the same size as the other boards mentioned in Scripture. Scripture therefore separates these boards and says, thus shall it be for them both (v. 24), that is, only for them and not for any of the other boards. The tabernacle was erected by utilizing these two boards. The remaining six boards were placed in the middle. The width of the tabernacle was thus ten cubits. We do not know if the corner boards were square or round, for we have only one remaining cubit. According to Rabbi Solomon’s explanation, these boards did not stand in a straight line because half a cubit was inside the tabernacle. We are dealing with boards, not with garments. They then set up the boards on the northern and southern sides. Now an amount equivalent to the thickness of the boards protruded from the tabernacle. The pillar of the opening of the tabernacle was therefore opposite it. The half a curtain of goatskin fixed it.

AND THOU SHALT REAR UP THE TABERNACLE. Moses should tell this to the wise-hearted. Or, Scripture states, And thou shalt rear up the tabernacle because Moses reared it up first. However, there were others with him, for many people were required to rear up the tabernacle.

AND THOU SHALT MAKE A VEIL. We find that Solomon acted similarly with regard to the opening of the Holy of Holies. The wall was possibly made out of wood. Scripture notes that the entire house measured sixty cubits, and Rashi, of blessed memory, explains the Holy measured forty cubits and the Holy of Holies twenty cubits. The sockets were made of silver out of respect for the ark. The Holy of Holies in the temple was double that of the one in the tabernacle in length, width, and height. Do not be astonished that Scripture writes that the temple was thirty cubits in height and the Holy of Holies took up a third of the temple. For there were upper stories directly above the ark cover that is over the Holy of Holies. The Book of Chronicles tells us, And he overlaid the upper chambers with gold (II Chron. 3:9).

AND THE VEIL SHALL DIVIDE UNTO YOU. The word ve-hivdilah (shall divide) is irregular in that it is ultimately accented. The same is true of the word ve-hikkita (and thou shalt smite) in and thou shalt smite the rock (Ex. 17:6).

AND THOU SHALT MAKE A SCREEN…THE WORK OF THE WEAVER. Ma’aseh rokem (the work of the weaver) is inferior to ma’aseh chosev (the work of the skillful workman). The pillars were covered with gold and the hooks were likewise covered with gold of respect for God. The sockets of the pillars were made out of brass because the screen was in between.
AND THOU SHALT MAKE. Any shape whose length is the same size as its width is called a square. The latter is a true square, as quadrilaterals come in five shapes.

[AND THE HEIGHT THEREOF SHALL BE THREE CUBITS.] Look, if contrary to the opinion of our sages, we say that there was no need for a ramp because the altar was three cubits high, what then will the opponents of the sages do with the altar which Solomon made? That altar was ten cubits high whereas the height of a person is only four cubits.
[FOUR-SQUARE.] Scripture describes the altar as being ravu’a (four-square) because the length of the altar was the same as its width.
CORNERS. The word pinnot means corners.

[TO TAKE AWAY ITS ASHES.] The meaning of ledasheno is, to take away its ashes. The meaning of yedasheneh (accept the fat) in And accept the fat of thy burnt-sacrifice; Selah (Ps. 20:4) is, he shall make ashes out of it. Its meaning is that the sacrifice will be burnt on the altar and accepted. Observe the word tedashen (make fat) in maketh the bones fat (Prov. 15:30). They all belong to the same conjugational form, namely, the pi’el . The meaning of tedashen is to fatten, as in As for Asher, his bread shall be fat (Gen. 49:20).
AND ITS SHOVELS. The word ve-ya’av (and its shovels) is similar to the word ve-ya’ah (shall sweep away) in And the hail shall sweep away (Is. 28:17).

[ALL THE VESSELS THEREOF.] The lamed in le-khol (all) in le-khol kelav (all the vessels thereof) is superfluous. It is like the lamed in le-min (from) in from the day that the foundation of the Lord’s temple was laid (Haggai 2:18).
A GRATING. The word mikhbar (a grating) is similar in meaning to the word kevarah (sieve) (Amos 9:9).
BRASS. The word brass (nechoshet) is connected [to the word grating ]. The text should be interpreted as if it read, a grating of brass, constructed like a net.
[LEDGE.] The word karkov (ledge) does not appear in any other place.

[HOLLOW WITH PLANKS.] Nevuv luchot (hollow with planks) is to be explained in accordance with the Aramaic translation. The phrase ve-ish nevuv yillavev (But an empty man will get understanding) (Job 11:12) is similar, for ish nevuv means an empty person, that is, a person lacking intelligence. The verse is similar to the aphorism, a head without a brain. The laver is not mentioned because it was not made from the gifts which were donated by all of Israel. It was made only from the gifts of the women. Hence the basin was mentioned with the chapter dealing with the spices, for the spices were also not donated by all of Israel. The spices were given only by the princes.

AND THOU SHALT MAKE. We find that Scripture says, kedemah mizrachah (on the east side eastward) (v. 13). We know that there are three “heads” to the east. The first is opposite the point of the head of Capricorn, which is the furthermost southern position of the sun. The second is opposite the celestial equator, which is the head of Aries and Libra. The third is opposite the head of Cancer, which is the sun’s furthermost northern position. The same applies to the phrase negbah temanah (south…southward) in the south.
SOUTHWARD. The word temanah (southward) comes from the same root as yamin (south). Compare, The north and the south (yamin), Thou hast created them (Ps. 89:13).

[AND THEIR FILLETS.] The meaning of chashukehem (their fillets) is their attachments, the hooks being attached to the pillars. Va-tidbak nafsho (and his soul did cleave) (Gen. 34:3) means the same as chashekah nafsho (his soul longeth) (Gen. 34:8).

AND FOR THE BREADTH…FIFTY CUBITS. The width of the courtyard was thus half of its length. The commentaries tell us that the tabernacle was placed fifty cubits westward. Now its width was fifty cubits. This is what and the breadth fifty every where (v. 18) means. However, I believe that the meaning of the breadth fifty every where is that the courtyard was a right-angled parallelogram, and its width was fifty cubits on all sides. There is no necessity to explain the breadth fifty every where as referring to the side of the courtyard, as Scripture does not repeat the dimensions length by width as it normally does.

ALL. The meaning of All the instruments of the tabernacle is, all the instruments that were for the use of the tabernacle. The pins of the tent and the pins of the court were of brass. So were the hammers.

If your heart desires to know the truth Look at the body, And consider the most glorious thing in it. I will secretly reveal the mystery of the Urim and Thummim In the Torah portion entitled, And Thou Shalt Command .

AND THOU SHALT COMMAND. I will first note the reason for the position of this Torah portion. After God finished enumerating all the holy utensils, the veil, the tabernacle, the tent, the cover, the altar of the burnt offering, the courtyard, and the screen, He commenced to deal with those who ministered in the tabernacle. He explained the service which they alone were to perform. No stranger was permitted to perform the service alongside them. God opened with the command that they cause a lamp to burn using pure olive oil. They were not to employ any other oil. It is only fitting that those who ministered in the tabernacle were to be distinguished and set apart, both in family and in dress. Scripture lists the garments one after the other. Scripture then mentions that those who served in the tabernacle were obligated to learn the service during the seven days of consecration. Moses was to teach and train them. After this, the priests would serve in the tabernacle. They would offer the daily burnt offering on the altar of the burnt offering. They were not to offer it upon the golden altar. The priests were to offer only incense upon the golden altar and to make atonement upon its horns once a year.

And thou shalt command means that there is an eternal command upon the congregation to continually provide olive oil to kindle a perpetual light. Do not be troubled by the oil which the princes brought. It was anointing oil. The congregation, on the other hand, was obligated to bring oil for the light. There is a practice in countries where olives grow to choose pure olives, that is, olives that do not have any rot on them or olives that have not been partially eaten. These olives are then used to make oil for the king’s food. This is the reason that Scripture mentions pure before beaten .
FOR THE LIGHT. For the light needed during the night.
TO CAUSE A LAMP TO BURN. To kindle the lamps. Scripture states, that they should burn according to the ordinance (II Chron. 4:20) concerning Solomon’s candelabra.

[CONTINUALLY.] The meaning of tamid (continually) is nightly. There is a more difficult usage of the term tamid , namely, and it shall be always (tamid) upon his forehead (Ex. 28:38). The meaning of the latter is that the holy plate shall always be upon the miter whenever the miter is placed upon the head of the high priest.

WHICH IS BEFORE THE TESTIMONY. The testimony is short for the ark of testimony. Yefet says that ya’arokh (shall set) is similar in meaning to ke-erkekha (as thou valuest it) in as thou the priest valuest it (Lev. 27:12). It means that the priest shall estimate the amount of oil that will be sufficient for the lamps to give light from evening till morning. The same applies to the phrase nerot ha-ma’arakha (even the lamps to be set in order) (Ex. 39:37). Ya’arokh may also be properly interpreted as meaning shall set, for the lamps were set in a semicircle. I will yet speak on this.

AND BRING THOU. Scripture says, And bring thou near unto thee [ Aaron thy brother, and his sons…that they may minister unto me ] because at first Moses was the high priest. I have already hinted at why Aaron was chosen to be sanctified to the Lord so that the priests would make atonement for Israel. Aaron was chosen because of the importance of Nahshon’s family. We cannot find fault with Moses, our master, as Moses was a fugitive. Who would have given him a Hebrew woman? Furthermore, the burden of all of Israel was upon Moses. Moses had to teach Israel the commandments. He also had to judge all difficult cases.

[THAT THEY MAY MINISTER UNTO ME.] The vav in lekhahano (that they minister) in that they may minister unto me is superfluous. It is like the vav in chayeto (beast) in every beast of the field (Ps. 104:11) and beno (son of) in the son of Beor (Num. 24:3). Our verse lists the sons of Aaron. It is possible that Aaron had other sons besides these. There is no doubt that Aaron’s family increased greatly in the wilderness. Hence they were given the many cities enumerated in the Book of Joshua.

AND THOU SHALT MAKE HOLY GARMENTS. They are called holy garments because they were worn during the sanctuary service. On the other hand, it is possible that they were called holy garments in accordance with that they sanctify not the people with their garments (Ezek. 44:19). The garments of Aaron referred to in our verse are the ones which Scripture later enumerates.
FOR SPLENDOUR AND FOR BEAUTY. They shall glorify themselves with these garments, for no other Israelite shall wear similar garments.
AND THOU SHALT. The vav in milletiv (I have filled) refers to lev (hearted).

AND THESE ARE THE GARMENTS. Scripture first mentions the breastplate, which was worn over the ephod, which was worn over the robe. It then mentions the tunic and the girdle which went around it after the mitre was placed on Aaron’s head. This is what happened when Aaron washed and put on linen breeches. However, there was no reason to mention the breeches here nor in the description of the actual investiture of Aaron, for it is the manner of all men to wear breeches. Now Moses put the tunic upon Aaron. He then placed the mitre upon Aaron’s head, and He placed “the plate of the holy crown” upon the mitre. Our verse, which enumerates the priestly garments, does not mention “the plate of the holy crown” because “the plate of the holy crown” was not a garment. However, our sages mentioned the holy plate among the priestly garments because most of the objects worn by the high priest were garments. Hence the sages speak of the eight garments worn by the high priest. The Urim and Thummim were not garments. Neither were the stones, nor the cards. After this Moses encircled Aaron with the girdle. Moses then placed the robe upon Aaron. He then placed the ephod upon the robe and put the ephod upon him, and he girded him with the skilfully woven band of the ephod and bound it unto him therewith (Lev. 8:7). The skillfully woven band was part of the ephod. The ephod was so called because of the skillfully woven band. Moses dressed Aaron according to the order described in our verse. Do not be bothered by the fact that Scripture later states, regarding the actual investiture of Aaron, And he set the mitre upon his head (Lev. 8:9). Its meaning is, he had already placed the mitre with the golden plate on Aaron’s head when he dressed him in the tunic. The meaning of and clothed him with garments (Zech. 3:5) is similar; i.e., they had already clothed him. For Scripture previously states, So they set a fair mitre upon his head ( Ibid .).
AND THEY SHALL TAKE THE GOLD. The wise-hearted who made the priestly garments were trustworthy.

AND THEY SHALL MAKE THE EPHOD. Scripture starts with the ephod because it was larger than the breastplate. The Torah tells us that the breastplate be not loosed from the skilfully woven band of the ephod (v. 28). There are some very difficult questions relating to the ephod and the breastplate. Moses only made one ephod. However, Scripture states, that he came down with an ephod in his hand (I Sam. 23:6). The latter does not refer to the ephod made by Moses, for Scripture does not read “the ephod,” the meaning of which is, the well-known ephod, as it does when it states, “Bring hither the ephod” (I Sam. 23:9). Furthermore, why does Scripture state, he came down , but it does not say he brought down? It thus appears that the ephod was accidentally among his possessions. Additionally, Scripture there states, fourscore persons that did wear a linen (bad) ephod (I Sam. 22:18). Many commentaries explain this verse as meaning that the persons were fit to wear the ephod. However, they did not bother to learn the truth. A bad (linen) ephod is an ephod made from a type of flax. However, the ephod made by Moses was not made of bad (linen). It was made of gold, blue wool, purple wool, and scarlet, with shesh (linen) intertwined with all of the aforementioned. They only inquired of the breastplate of judgment which had the Urim and Thummim upon it. Scripture similarly writes, by the judgment of the Urim before the Lord (Num. 27:21). Bring hither the ephod (I Sam. 23:9) does not present a counterargument because the breastplate was connected to it. The Urim went along with the breastplate. We similarly read, till there stood up a priest with Urim and Thummim (Neh. 7:65). Scripture likewise states, Thy Thummim and Thy Urim (Deut. 33:8). Now, Scripture tells us that God answered David through Abiathar’s ephod. However, we also read that when Saul went to war he inquired of the Urim (I Sam. 28:6). These were the very Urim that were placed in the breastplate of judgment which was with the ephod and the ark. However, David inquired of Abiathar’s ephod in Ziklag. Abiathar’s ephod was thus not Moses’ ephod. The following problem is even more difficult. It is clear that the Urim do not refer to the stones of the breastplate, as Scripture openly states, And thou shalt set in it settings of stones (v. 17). The setting of the stones was the work of a stonecutter and not the work of Moses. God then told Moses, And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim (v. 30). Scripture, in describing the making of the breastplate, tells us, And they set in it four rows of stones (Ex. 39:10). Scripture then describes the four rows of stones. Scripture tells us that Moses placed the breastplate upon Aaron and in the breastplate he put the Urim and the Thummim (Lev. 8:8). Now according to the plain meaning of the text the stones were not the objects that enlightened or fulfilled, because inquiries were made of the Urim and Thummim. We do not know what they were. The explanation that the names of the tribes and the patriarchs were inscribed on the breastplate is of no help, for the breastplate of judgment was so called only because of the Urim that were on it. There is an additional question: we cannot identify the Urim with the Thummim, for Scripture states, with Urim and Thummim (Neh. 7:65). Furthermore, the words with Urim and Thummim are in the plural. They thus consisted of many objects. Rabbi Solomon says that the Urim and Thummim consisted of an inscription of God’s explicit name. However, he would not have said this had he seen the responsa of Rabbi Hai Gaon. There is a very deep secret behind the ephod and the breastplate. I will allude only to a part of this secret. Perhaps he who knows the mind of the Most High will understand it. The following are the keys to the secret of the ephod. The two wreathen chains on the two rings [represent the head of Aries and Libra]. The band of the ephod represents the celestial equator. Hence six names were inscribed on the stone which was on the other shoulder. Now these things can only be grasped by the mind. Hence six names were inscribed on one stone in accordance with the number, names, and order of birth of the tribes of the children of Israel. Six names were similarly inscribed on the second stone. On the other hand, the names on the breastplate were not divided in the same manner as they are grasped by the mind. They were divided in a way that could be perceived by the eye. Scripture states, And they shall bind the breastplate by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod with a thread of blue (v. 28) to prevent the breastplate from moving to the side. The breastplate was folded, for the Urim and Thummim were kept there until such time as they were needed. They were then placed outside of the breastplate. Note, the stones of the ephod were like each other. They were of one color. This was not the case with the stones of the breastplate, for the sapphire stones served as a memorial, while the judgment of the children of Israel was upon the stones of the breastplate. The word Urim is related to the word ur (fire) in I am warm, I have seen the fire (Is. 44:16). The Thummim are so called because they are whole. The Urim were of gold and silver. This was not the case with the Thummim. The [importance of the] number [twelve] has been established by irrefutable proof from the upper and lower worlds. The intelligent will understand what I say. Now the priests had many ephodim. They all had bands. However, they lacked the breastplate and the Urim. A priest who was an expert in using the Urim and Thummim was able to respond to an inquirer because the ephod at hand resembled [the ephod made by Moses]. However, the priest did not always get an answer. Now if I wanted to even begin to reveal this secret it would take up more space than the entire commentary which I have composed on this book. For only an individual who has studied works on geometry and the secret of the way the sky works can understand the secret of the ephod. There is no need to expand on the form of the ephod, the breastplate, and the rings.

ONYX STONES. The avne shoham (onyx stones) were white. They are called burla in Aramaic and balor in Arabic. We have no way to positively identify the stones that were set in the breastplate. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon translated them as he saw fit, as he had no tradition to rely upon. We read the Gaon’s translation and noticed that he rendered sappir (sapphire) as white. However, this is not the case. Sappir is red. The fact that the first stone mentioned by the Torah was a carnelian does not refute this, for there are five visible colors: white, lightning, red, green, and black. Now since red is the middle color it comes in various shades. Saadiah Gaon renders nofekh (carbuncle) as black on the basis of and she painted (ba-pukh) her eyes (II Kings 9:30). However, the nun in nofekh is undoubtedly a root letter, for nofekh follows the paradigm of odem (carnelian). A great Sephardic scholar said that yahalom (emerald) is a diamond. This stone has the ability to break up all other stones and to bore through bdellium. Yahalom is related to the word holem (smiteth) in smiteth the anvil (Is. 41:7). The yod of yahalom is not a root letter. It is like the yod of yitzhar (oil). Also achlamah (amethyst) is to be identified with the dream stone. This is a stone that always induces dreams in the person who wears it. One should not be surprised at this, as every stone has a specific power placed in it by nature. Thus there is a stone that attracts iron. There is likewise a stone that stops bleeding. Another stone is repelled by vinegar. There is also a stone whose pieces always form a triangle when broken.

CHAINS. The middle root letter has been doubled in sharsherot (chains). However, the word has the same meaning when the middle root letter is not doubled. Compare, sharshot gavlut (plaited chains) (v. 22). It is very difficult to explain the meaning of gavlut (plaited) in Hebrew. The same applies to many of the words employed by Scripture that refer to the making of the breastplate as well as to the word choshen (breastplate) itself.
AND THEY SHALL BIND. Ve-yirkesu is related to the word me-rukhse (from the plottings) in from the plottings of man (Ps. 31:21). It means twisted.
AND THOU SHALT PUT IN THE BREASTPLATE OF JUDGMENT. Judgment refers to the laws of God and his decrees concerning the future. It is these things that people inquire of the Urim and Thummim.

AND THOU SHALT MAKE. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon translates the word me’il (robe) by the Arabic memtar , which is a cloak-like garment except that its opening was in the midst of the robe. Our sages said that the pomegranates (v. 33) were placed all around the robe. A bell was placed between every two pomegranates. However, others say that the bells were not visible. They were placed inside the pomegranates, where they rang.

AND THOU SHALT MAKE A PLATE. The Gaon renders tzitz (plate) atzabah . It was placed on the mitre. It was not shaped like a crown, as the plate was placed only on the forehead. According to the plain meaning of the text, the migba’ot (head-tires) (Lev. 8:13) were not shaped like the mitre ( mitznefet ). The head-tires are similar to the high hats which men in this and surrounding countries place upon their heads as a head covering. [37.] THE MITRE. The mitre is made from long thin material which is twisted only around the head. The turbans worn by women in these areas are somewhat similar. In Spain, Africa, Egypt, Babylonia, and Baghdad and in the land of the Ishmaelites, only men of respect, not the women, wear turbans on their heads. The important officials place a golden plate on the turban over the forehead. I have already noted that the ornaments in the Land of Israel and the customs practiced there differ from those in these areas. Rabbi Solomon found it necessary to harmonize Scripture by explaining that three blue threads were attached to the plate. However, according to the plain meaning of the text only one blue thread was necessary to keep the plate, which was on the face of the mitre on the forehead, in place.

AND THOU SHALT PUT IT ON A THREAD OF BLUE. The meaning of al petil techelt (on a thread of blue) is, with a thread of blue, as the thread was tied to the plate on two sides. There is no doubt that the front of the mitre was placed over the forehead. It was not placed over the head. Scripture elsewhere states, And they tied unto it a thread of blue, to fasten it upon the mitre (Ex. 39:31), that is, upon the forehead. Do not be surprised that Scripture uses the term al . We find the same in the following, And they came, both men with (al) women (Ex. 35:22); And the priest shall wave them with (al) the bread of the first-fruits for a wave-offering before the Lord (Lev. 23:20); with (al) the two lambs ( Ibid .); the fat with (al) the breast (Lev. 7:30). There are many similar instances in Scripture. Now you will never find [the mitre and the head-tires interchanging]. For the mitre was set aside only for Aaron, and the head-tires for his children. Some say that the word migba’ot (head-tires) is related to the word givot (hills) (Gen. 49:26). The mitre surrounded and wrapped the head. We similarly read, He will violently roll (tzanof) and toss thee Like a ball (yitznofkha tzenefah) (Is. 22:18); Yea, He will wind thee round and round (ve-otekha ato) (Is. 22:17). The one who knows how the mitre is wrapped knows the meaning of [ The mitre shall be removed… ] this shall be no more the same: that which is low shall be exalted, and that which is high abased (Ezek. 21:31). It takes a special skill to wind a mitre around the head. Now Scripture states, And thou shalt set the mitre upon his head, and put the holy crown upon the mitre (Ex. 29:6). The tzitz (plate) (v. 36) is thus called a nezer (crown). But upon himself shall his crown (nizro) shine (yatzitz) is similar (Ps. 132:18). Perhaps they all are used in the sense of tzitz , meaning something seen. The same is true with the word metzitz (peereth) in He peereth through the lattice (Cant. 2:9). Note that the five senses come together in the two cavities which are in that part of the brain which is behind the forehead. This is where the imaginative power is located. Furthermore, all thoughts begin there. It is for this reason that Scripture writes, regarding the plate, that Aaron shall bear the iniquity committed in the holy things (v. 38). It is possible that those who hallowed holy things unto the Lord did so while thinking improper thoughts.

AND THOU SHALT WEAVE THE TUNIC IN CHEQUER WORK. When Scripture first mentions Aaron’s tunic it says, a tunic of chequer work (v. 4). Only Aaron’s tunic was chequered. His sons’ tunics were not. The tunic was chequered to dignify Aaron. Scripture similar reads, And he put upon him the tunic (Lev. 8:7) when it describes Aaron’s investiture. It reads, the tunic , the reference being to the chequered tunic. However, concerning Aaron’s children we read, and clothed them with tunics (Lev. 8:13). The latter is similar to And for Aaron’s sons thou shalt make tunics (v. 40). Rabbi Saadiah Gaon translated ve-shibatzta (and thou shalt weave…in chequer work) as: you shall weave eye-like [designs]. It is a coin-like design, that is, a square within a circle.

AND THOU SHALT PUT THEM UPON AARON THY BROTHER. The word otam (them) takes in the chequered tunic, the mitre, and the girdle which are Aaron’s garments. It also takes in the unchequered tunics, the girdles, and the head-tires which are the garments of Aaron’s sons.
AND CONSECRATE THEM. By word of mouth. It is similar to the priest shall make him unclean (Lev. 13:44).
LINEN BREECHES. The linen breeches were short so that the priest would not trip over them.
WHEN THEY GO IN. To offer incense or to kindle the lamps.
AND THIS IS THE THING THAT THOU SHALT DO UNTO THEM. To Aaron and his sons.

[TAKE.] There is no difference between lekach (take) and kach (take). We find the same to be true of tzak (pour out) and yetzak (pour) in Pour out (tzak) for the people, that they may eat (II Kings 4:41) and in And also pour (yetzak) water into it (Ezek. 24:3).

[ONE YOUNG BULLOCK.] The fact that Scripture notes that the par (bull) was a ben bakar (of the herd) indicates that the par (bull) was young. The same applies to the phrase bene yonah (turtle-doves) (Lev. 1:14), and the phrase se’_ir izzim (a goat) (Lev. 4:23).
[AND TWO RAMS.] An ayal (ram) is older than a keves (lamb). The fact that the drink offering for an ayal (ram) consists of a third of a hin and that of a keves (lamb) a quarter of a hin proves this.
AND UNLEAVENED…CAKES. They were thick, as wafers unleavened proves.

[WITH OIL.] Scripture reads ba-shemen (with oil). The reference, in keeping with the rule, is to olive oil. [Of FINE WHEATEN FLOUR.] The word solet (fine flour) refers to flour made from wheat cleansed of all impurities. It is called samid in Arabic. It is produced in the land of the Ishmaelites. There is no better bread than bread made from it. Many connect the word solet to the word salita (thou hast trodden) in Thou hast trodden light all them that err from Thy statutes (Ps. 119:118); and to sillah (trodden) in The Lord hath trodden All my mighty men in the midst of me (Lam. 1:15). They say that makkolet (food) in food to your household (I Kings 5:25) is similar. Others say that solet means ground.
AND BRING THEM IN THE BASKET. You shall bring the bread, which is in the basket as the law requires, to the door of the tent of meeting. The same applies to the bullock and the rams.
AND THOU SHALT TAKE THE GARMENTS. The breastplate ( choshen ) is called a garment because it covers that part of the body which lies opposite the heart.

AND THOU SHALT SET. It is also not beyond the realm of possibility that Moses placed the mitre on Aaron last. Scripture mentions the mitre before the girdle at the opening of the Torah portion because the mitre is more important than the girdle.

HIS HEAD. Only on Aaron’s head, as he was the anointed priest. Now Aaron was anointed before the mitre was placed on his head, for Moses poured the oil only upon the head. We similarly read, It is like the precious oil upon the head, Coming down upon the beard; Even Aaron’s beard (Ps. 133:2).
AND THOU SHALT BRING HIS SONS. To the door of the tent of meeting.

AND THOU SHALT GIRD THEM WITH GIRDLES. Girdles takes in Aaron’s girdle and the girdle of his sons. Similarly the breeches. After stating them , Scripture goes on to explain that the reference is to Aaron and his sons. It is similar to And she opened it, and saw it, even the child (Ex. 2:6).
[AND BIND.] The word ve-chavashta (and bind) is similar to the word chovesh (healer) in I will not be a healer (Is. 3:7).

AND THOU SHALT CONSECRATE. The one who translated the Torah into Aramaic is of the opinion that u-milleta yad (and thou shalt consecrate) is similar to u-milu yadav (so shall they consecrate it) (Ezek. 43:26). However, what shall we do with milu yedkhem ha-yom (consecrate yourselves today to the Lord) (Ex. 32:29)? Saadiah Gaon explains the word yad to mean obligation. Others say that the term melu’im (consecration) is used because it indicates that they are complete, full, and trained. However, what will they do with u-mile’u yadav (so shall they consecrate it) (Ezek. 43:26)?

AND THOU SHALT BRING THE BULLOCK. This has already been mentioned. Its meaning is as follows. When you shall bring the bullock, Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon it. Some say that the meaning of and Aaron shall lay is: Aaron alone shall first lay his hands upon the head of the bullock. His sons shall then do the same. Now with regard to the ram, Scripture later states, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram (v. 15). Scripture thus describes exactly what happened. They should lay their hands together, not one after the other.
AND THOU SHALT KILL THE BULLOCK. Moses slaughtered the bullock.

[BEFORE THE LORD.] Scripture reads, before the Lord, because the ark was in the center of the western side of the tabernacle. The incense altar was directly aligned with it. So was the altar of the burnt offerings.
HE SHALL POUR OUT. The priest who pours shall pour out.
AND THOU SHALT TAKE. Bullock and goats do not have a fat tail ( alyah ).

[KIDNEYS.] Some say that kelayot (kidneys) are so called because the word kelayot is related to the word kaletah (pineth) in My soul yearneth, yea even pineth for the courts of the Lord (Ps. 84:3). For the power of sexual desire is located in the kidneys.
BUT THE FLESH OF THE BULLOCK. Flesh takes in the head and the pieces of the bullock.
AND ITS DUNG. Logically speaking, it was to be washed and then it was to be burned.. AND HE SHALL MAKE THEM SMOKE ( ve-hiktir ). The reference is to the enumerated organs.

[SIN-OFFERING.] A sin offering is called a chatat because it is brought to atone for a sin. The same applies to the asham (guilt-offering). Hence the meaning of ve-chitte’u et ha-mizbe’ach (they shall purify the altar) is: they shall remove the sin from the altar.
THOU SHALT ALSO TAKE THE ONE RAM. Any one of the two rams which you decide to choose.

AND THOU SHALT SLAY THE RAM, AND THOU SHALT TAKE ITS BLOOD AND DASH IT ROUND ABOUT AGAINST THE ALTAR. Not on the corners of the altar. Look, he [Moses] shall dash all the blood round about against the altar and not upon the base of the altar.
AND THE RAM. Scripture does not mention that Moses was commanded to cut the bullock into pieces. It was therefore entirely burned. Hence Scripture does not mention the bullock’s legs.
AND WASH. By command.
AND THOU SHALT MAKE THE WHOLE RAM SMOKE. Hence the fat tail and the fat are not mentioned.
AND THOU SHALT TAKE. This second ram served as the ram of consecration.
THEN THOU SHALT KILL…TIP. The word tenukh (tip) has no counterpart. Saadiah Gaon says that it refers to the soft tissue which is connected to the circle of the ear.
THE GREAT TOE. The plural of bohen (great toe) is behonot (Jud. 1:6). This is grammatically inconsistent. This noun is thus vocalized according to two paradigms. There are many such nouns.
[AND DASH THE BLOOD.] The blood of the second ram shall be dashed like the blood of the first ram. The reference is only to the remaining blood.
AND THOU SHALT TAKE OF THE BLOOD THAT IS UPON THE ALTAR…AND SPRINKLE IT UPON AARON, AND UPON HIS GARMENTS. Beneath his garments and upon his garments.
AND THOU SHALT TAKE OF THE RAM THE FAT. The reference is to the fat that is upon the innards, as stated in the Torah portion Va-Yikra .

THE RIGHT THIGH. The thigh that is on the right side and the breast were taken from the ram of consecration. From that day on, the thigh and the breast of peace offerings were to be given to Aaron and his sons. However, Moses alone ate the breast of the ram of consecration because he was a high priest.
AND ONE LOAF OF BREAD. The reference is to the unleavened bread (v. 2).
AND SHALT WAVE THEM. While they are in the hands of Aaron and his sons.
AND THOU SHALT TAKE THEM FROM THEIR HANDS. Our verse states, from their hands . Elsewhere Scripture states, from off their hands (Lev. 8:28). They mean the same thing.
A SWEET SAVOUR. The chet is doubled in nicho’ach (sweet savour). [A SWEET SAVOUR BEFORE THE LORD.] The one who understands the secret of man’s soul will understand this.
AN OFFERING. The word issheh (offering) is an adjective. It is related to the word esh (fire). Scripture elsewhere states, from the fire (Num. 18:9).
AND THOU SHALT TAKE. From Aaron’s ram. Aaron’s sons are not mentioned, as Aaron was the principal.
[PORTION.] The word manah means a portion.

AND THOU SHALT SANCTIFY. From this day and henceforth. Waving and heaving are not identical. For what is heaved is lifted up. It is not waved. The meaning of even their heave-offering (v. 28) is: the heave offerings which they will separate from peace offerings, shall be heaved in honor of God.
AND THE HOLY GARMENTS OF AARON SHALL BE FOR HIS SONS AFTER HIM. Shall be for his son who is anointed in his place.
[AFTER HIM.] After his death.

SEVEN DAYS. The word yilbasham (put them on) is vocalized with a long rather than a short kamatz . The word amilam (I will cut them off) in Verily, in the name of the Lord I will cut them off (Ps. 118:10) is similar.
AND SEETHE. By command. It is similar to and thou shalt smite the rock (Ex. 17:6), and to So Solomon built the house (I Kings 6:14).
AND AARON AND HIS SONS SHALL EAT. The bread remaining in the basket.
AND THEY SHALL EAT THOSE THINGS. The verse is abridged.
[THEM.] The word otam (them) also refers to something else.
BUT A STRANGER. Who is not of Aaron’s seed.
AND IF AUGHT. The ram of consecration is so called because they are consecrated by it.

THEE. The word otakhah has an etnach beneath it. Otakhah is a combination of otakh (thee) (Gen. 39:9), which is vocalized with a long kamatz beneath the tav , and otekha (thee) in for thee have I seen (Gen. 7:1).
AND EVERY DAY SHALT THOU OFFER THE BULLOCK. Every day of the seven days of consecration.

[BESIDE THE OTHER OFFERINGS OF ATONEMENT.] Its meaning is, in addition to the two rams. Scripture further states, As hath been done this day, so the Lord hath commanded to do , to make atonement for you (Lev. 8:34).
MOST HOLY. The meaning of kodesh kodashim (most holy) is holy like any other holy object.

WHATSOEVER TOUCHES THE ALTAR SHALL BE HOLY. This is similar to Whatsoever shall touch the flesh thereof shall be holy (Lev. 6:20). Some say that the verse speaks only of the bread. Scripture is telling us that if the bread is not holy, that is, if the bread is unclean, then it shall not touch the altar.

NOW THIS IS. Its meaning is: now this is the sacrifice. Similarly, the meaning of This they shall give (Ex. 30:13) is: this amount they shall give. Similarly And this is that thou shalt make it (Gen. 6:15). Moses shall do this during the seven days of consecration. Afterwards Aaron and his sons shall do likewise.

THE ONE LAMB. The heh prefixed to the word keves (lamb) also serves as a prefix to the word echad (one). The phrase is to be read as if written, et ha-keves ha-echad (the one lamb). Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that the meaning of et ha-keves echad is, the lamb, one lamb.
A TENTH PART. A tenth part of an ephah .
[A HIN.] Also note that hin is an Egyptian measure.
AND. The word u-kheniskah (and according to the drink offering thereof) refers to boker (morning).

IT SHALL BE A CONTINUAL BURNT-OFFERING THROUGHOUT YOUR GENERATIONS. They shall bring these offerings when they enter the land of Canaan. For the Israelites offered burnt offerings only for fifty days in the desert of Sinai. This is what Scripture means by It is a continual burnt-offering, which was offered in mount Sinai (Num. 28:6). The tabernacle was placed at the edge of the camp at the bottom of the mount, as the tribes were intermingled. On the first day of the second month they began to know the number of each tribe and to make standards (Num. 1 and 2). After they traveled a distance of a three-day journey from Mount Sinai, the ark journeyed in the midst of the camps (Num. 10:33). Logically speaking, the Israelites offered burnt offerings and sacrifices only at Sinai and on Yom Kippur in the second year. This is what Scripture states regarding Aaron’s service. The Torah there writes, And he [Aaron] did as the Lord commanded Moses (Lev. 16:34). Scripture similarly states, Did ye bring unto Me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, O house of Israel? (Amos 5:25). Israel spent about thirty-eight years in a wasteland, in a howling wilderness (Deut. 32:10). Where did they get half a hin of olive oil and a half hin of wine daily? How could they carry almost fourteen thousand hin around with them? Where did they get two lambs daily in the first year? Where did they get the animals for the additional sacrifices on the Sabbath and the festivals? The statement we and our cattle (Num. 20:4) does not refute our contention, for Israel was then at Kadesh, and they bought cattle from the settled population. Furthermore, they looted the Midianites and the lands of Sihon and Og in that year. They thus had an abundance of cattle.
[I WILL MEET.] Scripture clearly explains the reason that the tabernacle is called the ohel mo’ed (the tent of meeting).
WITH YOU. Israel. We find this to be the case when the congregation was called together.

TO SPEAK THERE UNTO THEE. To speak there alone to you. However, Yefet says that the meaning of I will meet with you is: with Moses and occasionally with Aaron. He maintains that to speak there unto thee hints that God will continually speak there with Moses. He offers, And there I will meet with the children of Israel (v. 43) as proof.

AND [THE TENT] SHALL BE SANCTIFIED BY MY GLORY. I believe that the tent of meeting was the place of meeting because it took in everything, namely, the tabernacle and all its utensils, the ark, and the three objects. The tent will be sanctified by My glory, which will rest on the cherubim.

AND I WILL SANCTIFY THE TENT OF MEETING. It is because of the glory that the tent is holy, for it was sanctified by the glory. The altar that stood before the opening of the tent of meeting was similarly sanctified.
AARON ALSO AND HIS SONS WILL I SANCTIFY. I will sanctify Aaron and his sons, who minister in the tent of meeting and upon the altar.

AND I WILL DWELL. Scripture describes how God’s glory will dwell among the children of Israel when the standards will be set up. Four standards were set up on the four sides. Additionally, there was a separation between the camp of the Levites and the camp of the Israelites because they too camped on all four sides, There was another barrier beyond this barrier where the tent of meeting was placed amidst the children of Israel. Now a person who experienced a seminal emission did not have to leave the camp of Israel. Neither was there a place set aside beyond the border of the camp for a person to sit down [and relieve himself]. The commandment for a person who experienced a seminal emission to leave the camp applied only to the camp of Israel when it went to war against the enemy. The commandment When thou goest forth in camp against thine enemies (Deut. 23:10) similarly does not speak of the entire camp of Israel, men, women, and children. It is only males, and then only a small number of them, who sally out to wage war. Now when the soldiers of Israel carried the ark with them as Phineas did, they were unable to set up a barrier between themselves and the place of the ark.

AND THEY SHALL KNOW. Its meaning is, then they shall know that the only reason that I took them out of Egypt was so that they would make a sanctuary for Me that I may dwell among them. This is what Scripture means by ye shall serve God upon this mountain (Ex. 3:12).

AND THOU SHALT MAKE AN ALTAR TO BURN INCENSE UPON. The word miktar (to burn) is an infinitive. It is like the word u-mishlo’ach (and of sending) in and of sending portions one to another (Esth. 9:19).
A CUBIT. The altar was a half a cubit higher than the table. Perhaps it was similarly half a cubit higher than the menorah. The altar was aligned with the cherubim which spread their wings upward.

AND THOU SHALT OVERLAY IT WITH PURE GOLD. A top is mentioned with regard to the altar of incense. Scripture does not mention a top with regard to the brass altar. The altar was called the golden altar because it was overlaid with gold. The same applies to The pure table (Lev. 24:6). It is like the pure candlestick (Lev. 24:4).
UPON THE TWO SIDES OF IT. Scripture states this in order to be especially clear.
[WHEREWITH.] THE heh at the end of the word ba-hemmah (wherewith) is superfluous, as I have already noted, since hemmah is penultimately accented.
AND THOU SHALT MAKE THE STAVES OF ACACIAWOOD. And overlay them with gold like the staves of the ark.
AND THOU SHALT PUT IT BEFORE THE VEIL. On the outside.
BEFORE THE ARK-COVER. The altar should be aligned with the ark cover.

AND AARON SHALL BURN THEREON INCENSE OF SWEET SPICES. Along with other spices ( besamim ). It is possible that the sammim (sweet spices) were the most important ingredient. It is also possible that Scripture mentions sammim (spices) in order to distinguish between the compounds, as one of the compounds consisted only of besamim (spices). It did not contain sammim (sweet spices).
[WHEN HE DRESSETH.] When he fixes the wick and the oil.
LIGHTETH THE LAMPS. Scripture employs be-he’alot for lighting because the flame of the wick goes up. Be-he’alot is clearly a transitive verb.
A PERPETUAL INCENSE. When they offer burnt offerings. Scripture therefore says, throughout your generations .
YE SHALL OFFER NO STRANGE INCENSE. An incense which is not its exact duplicate.
AND AARON SHALL MAKE ATONEMENT UPON THE HORNS OF IT ONCE IN THE YEAR. On the tenth day of the seventh month.

[OF ATONEMENT.] The reference is to the blood of the bullock and the blood of the he-goat. The aforementioned is a yearly obligation. There is no reason for Scripture to mention the blood of the bullock brought by the anointed high priest when he sins and the blood of the bullock brought by the congregation when they sin. For they are not placed on the horns of the altar at fixed times. They are placed there only on rare occasions.
May the name of the exalted God be eternally blessed. He did every good for Israel.
To His messenger He revealed every secret In the Torah portion called Ki Tissa .

[WHEN THOU TAKEST THE SUM.] Scripture begins to explain the law of the atonement money which each and every one is obligated to give. The atonement money was not a free will offering. Scripture makes mention of the atonement money here because it notes above that atonement shall be made [upon the horns of the altar of incense] once a year. The atonement money was, as I will explain, similarly to be given once a year. The description of the laver and its base follow next because they are not to be made from free will gifts of the congregation but only from the mirrors of the women who performed tasks. Scripture also mentions the anointing oil and the sweet incense, for the princes alone brought them. Now since Scripture mentions the anointing oil it mentions the vessels which were anointed. Scripture also mentions the great craftsman, the perfumer, and the one whose counsel guided those who constructed the entire tabernacle, namely, Bezalel and Oholiab [who was with him]. Scripture mentions the Sabbath in order to warn the Israelites at the beginning not to do God’s work on the Sabbath. Scripture next records the prayer offered by Moses before he came down from the mountain. However, it first had to mention the making of the golden calf so that we would know why Moses prayed. Scripture then tells of Moses’ descent from the mountain, the burning of the calf, and Moses’ return to the mountain to pray for Israel a second time. Scripture mentions that Moses’ anger caused him to move his tent outside the camp of Israel. However, some say that Scripture records what happened. Scripture then mentions Moses’ great glory, namely, that Moses saw God’s glory. It tells us that God then commanded Moses to descend and hew out tablets. It informs us that God inscribed the tablets a second time. Scripture mentions the conditions upon which God made a treaty with Israel. These conditions are recorded in the Torah portion Ve-Ellaeh Ha-Mishpatim . Scripture then mentions that the skin of Moses’ face shone when Moses came down from the mountain with the tablets of the covenant in his hand. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that the atonement money was an annual obligation upon Israel. It was obligatory whether their king counted them or not. Saadiah Gaon offers the census taken by Moses in the desert as proof. Saadiah says that the money collected was used for the congregational sacrifices, the construction of the laver, the making of the anointing oil, and the sweet incense. Part of it was also given to the Sanhedrin. Bezalel and Oholiab allude to this. [WHEN THOU TAKEST THE SUM.] It is customary for the accountants who are intimate with the details of an account to itemize upon pages. However they write the sum of all the items at the head of the page. Some say that the plague which occurred in the days of David struck because Israel did not offer a ransom for their soul. If this is true it refutes the opinion of Saadiah Gaon.

[WHEN THOU NUMBEREST THEM.] The meaning of that there be no plague among them, when thou numberest them is: if they do not give atonement money at the very moment of the numbering, a plague will strike. However, Yefet says it means that if they are numbered and do not give their ransom, they will fall before their enemies when they go to war.
THIS. This amount. It is similar to And this thou shalt make it (Gen. 6:15).

[EVERY ONE THAT PASSETH.] The meaning of every one that passeth is everyone who passes his twentieth year. Twenty years is about three weeks of years [almost twenty-one years]. A person’s mind is then fully developed. His body also no longer grows in height.
[GERAHS.] These gerahs refer to the pits of a carob.
EVERY ONE…THAT ARE NUMBERED. Pekudim (that are numbered) is active.
THE RICH. Scripture explains why the rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less. The reason for this is that the money is an atonement for one’s soul.
AND THOU SHALT TAKE…AND SHALT APPOINT IT FOR THE SERVICE OF THE TENT OF MEETING. This is explained in the Torah portion Ve-Ellah Pekude .
[THAT IT MAY BE A MEMORIAL FOR THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.] For the tabernacle stood only upon sockets which were made from the atonement money as a memorial for the children of Israel.
AND THE LORD SPOKE. A new section begins here.

AND THE BASE THEREOF. Kanno means the base thereof. The bases that Solomon made proves this. Now Scripture states that the laver was placed between the tent of meeting and the altar . This shows that the altar was not adjacent to the door of the tent but was close to it The altar was placed in the center and was aligned with the altar of incense. The laver was placed between the tent and the altar, towards one of the sides. However, Scripture does not mention this. It does not seem logical for the laver to be aligned with the altar of incense and thus be aligned with the ark cover.

SHALL WASH. Scripture mentions that the laver was necessary because of those who served in the tabernacle, namely, Aaron and his sons and their descendants. Moses is not now mentioned, as Moses alone used the laver as long as he lived. However, Scripture mentions Moses’ use of the laver when it describes the actual setting up of the laver.

WHEN THEY GO INTO THE TENT OF MEETING, THEY SHALL WASH WITH WATER. The meaning of yirchatzu mayim is they shall wash with water. The reason the hands and feet have to be washed is that they are the active parts of the body. There are many such instances.

**ורחצו (And they shall wash) -** He reiterated and mentioned it another time [he had already written so in verse 19], to instruct that they should do so always [for future generations]. Or, he mentioned this [to add a punishment to the warning, to indicate] that if they do not do so, they are liable to death [as it is stated 'and they shall not die'; and so Rashi explains].
MOREOVER THE LORD SPOKE. This is a section unto itself.

TAKE THOU ALSO UNTO THEE. Kach lekha (take unto thee) is similar to lekh leha (get thee out) (Gen. 12:1) and u-kechu lakhem tzon (and take you lambs) (Ex. 12:21). According to the plain meaning of the text, aseh lekha saraf (make thee a fiery serpent) (Num. 21:8) and also pesal lekha (hew thee) (Ex. 34:1) are similar, for such is the way of the Hebrew language.

[MYRRH.] The word mor (myrrh) is difficult. Saadiah Gaon translated it as musk. It thus does not come from trees even though it has a pleasant odor. Perhaps this is the reason Scripture separates it from the spices. For Scripture states, I have gathered my myrrh with my spice (Cant. 5:1). Myrrh is thus gathered. Those who provide musk say that it is produced in the throat of a deer. Behold, Scripture states, And my hands dropped with myrrh (Cant. 5:5). Perhaps this is the case when the myrrh is wet.

[THE CHIEF SPICES.] Scripture reads besamim rosh (the chief spices) to indicate that the top of each spice is to be taken. The top of the spice is of a much better quality than that which remains at the end. [AND OF SWEET CINNAMON.] Having said kinnemon (cinnamon), what reason is there for Scripture to add besem (sweet)? It is possible that Scripture reads, ve-kinnemon besem , because the cinnamon had to be of the best quality. The same also applies to the calamus. [HALF SO MUCH, EVEN TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY.] The ancients, of blessed memory, said that all the ingredients were of equal weight. We will accept what they say. However, we do not know why Scripture says, half so much even two hundred and fifty . I do not understand the reason for the halves for it is the practice in all of the lands of the Ishmaelites not to add even the weight of a mustard seed to anything being weighed. They most certainly do not add anything to any ingredient used in the work of a perfumer.
CASSIA. We know from tradition that kiddah is cassia.
AND THOU SHALT MAKE IT…A PERFUME COMPOUNDED AFTER THE ART OF THE PERFUMER. Rokach mirkachat (a perfume compounded after the art of the perfumer) is similar to miktar ketoret (to burn incense) (v. 1).
[IT SHALL BE A HOLY ANOINTING OIL.] This is what Scripture refers to next.
AND THOU SHALT ANOINT THEREWITH THE TENT OF MEETING. This includes the entire tabernacle. Our verse mentions the ark. the most important object in the tent of meeting.
AND THE TABLE. The table is mentioned first because it was the largest [object in the sanctuary] and it had many utensils. Scripture then mentions the menorah, which had many utensils.
AND THE ALTAR OF BURNT-OFFERING. It had many vessels.
AND THOU SHALT SANCTIFY. With the anointing oil.

[WHATSOEVER TOUCHETH THEM SHALL BE HOLY.] We can derive the meaning of whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy from If one bear hallowed flesh (Haggai 2:12), which, according to the plain meaning of the text, is be taken literally. The verse teaches: if holy flesh touches bread, pottage, wine, oil, or any food it becomes holy. The same applies to the altar of burnt offering, as Scripture also uses the term “most holy” regarding it.
AND THOU SHALT ANOINT AARON AND HIS SONS. Alone, no one else.
THIS SHALL BE A HOLY ANOINTING OIL. All oil made according to this composition shall be used to anoint the seed of Aaron.

SHALL IT NOT BE POURED. Rabbi Merinus says that yisakh (poured) has the same meaning as yusakh . Similarly, va-yisem (he was put) in and he was put in a coffin (Gen. 50: 26) has the same meaning as va-yusam . [UPON THE FLESH OF MAN SHALL IT NOT BE POURED.] Scripture states, Upon the flesh of man shall it not be poured because it was customary in Israel for men and also for women to anoint themselves with oil. For Scripture states, but thou shalt not anoint thyself with oil (Deut. 28:40). It is prohibited for a priest and certainly for anyone else to anoint themselves with this oil, for the anointing oil was poured upon the head of the anointed.
ACCORDING TO THE COMPOSITION THEREOF. Oil composed of the exact amount of the above-listed spices.

WHOSOEVER. The meaning of or whosoever putteth any of it on a stranger (zar) is: or whosoever putteth any of it on someone who is not of Aaron’s family. Saadiah Gaon, of blessed memory, says that Israel had a tradition that David and his seed should be anointed with the anointing oil. Other kings were not to be so anointed. The Gaon was compelled to explain thus because Zadok took some of the anointing oil that was in the tent of meeting and used it to anoint Solomon. Yefet says that on a stranger means on someone who is not an Israelite. However, he was mistaken, for Scripture states, and the stranger (zar) that draweth nigh shall be put to death (Num. 3:10). The meaning of the latter is: To the end that no stranger (zar), that is not of the seed of Aaron, draw near (Num. 17:5). Others say that this law refers only to the oil made by Moses. However, this also does not appear to me to be correct. For Scripture first states, This shall be a holy anointing oil unto Me throughout your generations (v. 31). Furthermore, the Pentateuch states (v. 33), Whosoever, compoundeth any like it , or whosoever putteth any of “a similarly compounded oil” upon a stranger . Thus there is no difference between the anointing oil made by Moses and its duplicate which was made later. Scripture does not state, “except for the family of David.” I believe that all the commandments are obligatory on all the generations of Israel. The law stating that no burnt offering should be offered in any but the chosen place is an example. Nevertheless, we find that Gideon, Samuel, and also Elijah at Mount Carmel brought burnt offerings. I mentioned Gideon because he offered burnt offerings even though he was not a priest. The same is true of Samuel. The fact that he was descended from Korah is of no avail. These acts were all based on temporary [ ad hoc ] rulings. We can say the same also with regard to Solomon. Solomon was anointed with the anointing oil on the temporary ruling of the prophet Nathan or Gad.

TAKE UNTO THEE SWEET SPICES. The ancients, of blessed memory, received a tradition that there were eleven types of spices. Now the verse that notes that spices were to be used in the sweet incense does not list the spices that were to be used in the sweet incense. Scripture mentions the sweet spices. However, Scripture does not mention their weight.
[SWEET SPICES.] Scripture mentions sammim (sweet spices) a second time because it wants to say: take the aforementioned sweet spices, and along with them, take pure frankincense.
OF EACH SHALL THERE BE A LIKE WEIGHT. Each spice to be compounded by itself. It shall then be mixed.

AND THOU SHALT MAKE…SEASONED WITH SALT. Memullach (seasoned with salt) means seasoned with salt from Sodom. Others say that memullach means thinly ground. Or it is related to the word melechah (salt) in A salt land ( Jer. 17:6).
AND THOU SHALT BEAT SOME OF IT VERY SMALL. As thin as you are able to make it. This is the perpetual incense which was offered on the golden altar.
AND THE INCENSE WHICH THOU SHALT MAKE. This alludes to Moses.
YE SHALL NOT MAKE. Israel is being spoken to.
IT SHALL BE UNTO THEE HOLY. The priest, or all of Israel. Remember the days of old (Deut. 32:7) is similar.
WHOSOEVER. Scripture first warns. It then mentions the punishment, as is the law.
